query: High-entropy alloys can combine mechanical strength, wear resistance, corrosion protection, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability, while their large compositional space offers opportunities to tune degradation in harsh environments. Prior studies have largely considered wear and corrosion separately, and only a few reports address their combined action, leaving the governing behavior poorly understood. For a high-entropy alloy subjected to tribo-corrosion, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the coupled response and why? Describe a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, predict changes in total degradation and its wear and corrosion components relative to a matched baseline, state where the prediction should hold or fail, connect it to the available prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy alloys under tribo-corrosion, the synergistic interplay between wear and corrosion arises because mechanical sliding continuously disrupts the passivating oxide film, exposing fresh metal which corrodes more rapidly. In turn, the localized corrosion degrades the surface microstructure, making it more susceptible to wear. This feedback loop produces overall degradation that is greater than the sum of individual wear and corrosion effects.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy with an intact, naturally formed passive oxide layer that initially confers corrosion protection.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled sliding wear test in a corrosive environment while maintaining a matched set of tests in inert (non-corrosive) environments.
generation.conditions: Perform three parallel sets of experiments: (1) wear-only in an inert liquid to minimize corrosion, (2) corrosion-only via static immersion in the corrosive fluid without mechanical stress, and (3) combined tribo-corrosion where sliding friction is conducted in the corrosive medium. Environmental parameters like temperature, pH, and electrolyte composition are held constant across tests.
generation.structural_mediator: The passivating oxide layer and its rate of mechanical removal and regeneration.
generation.mechanism: Mechanical sliding in a corrosive environment causes partial and repeated removal of the oxide layer. The exposed bare alloy then corrodes more rapidly. This corrosion further deteriorates the microstructure, lowering the surface’s wear resistance and making it even more vulnerable to mechanical damage, thereby intensifying both wear and corrosion in a mutually reinforcing manner.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under tribo-corrosion conditions, the total degradation (quantified by weight loss, increased corrosion current densities, or wear track depth) will be notably higher than the simple additive effect of wear-only and corrosion-only baseline measurements. Both the wear component and the corrosion component should individually show enhancement when compared to their performance in isolated tests.
generation.baseline: High-entropy alloy specimens tested separately under controlled wear-only conditions (in inert media) and corrosion-only conditions (static immersion in the corrosive solution).
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold in environments where the mechanical removal rate of the oxide passivation outpaces its ability to reform. In systems with rapid oxide healing kinetics or in alloys lacking a robust oxide layer, the synergistic feedback may not be present, and the mechanism would thus not dominate the degradation behavior.
generation.uncertainty: While the qualitative synergistic mechanism is anticipated, the exact magnitude of the increased degradation rate (whether it is, for instance, 10%, 50%, or 100% greater than the additive contributions) remains uncertain without precise experimental quantification and may vary significantly with the detailed composition and environmental conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of high-entropy alloy samples under identical initial conditions and subject them to three test environments: (a) sliding wear in an inert (non-corrosive) medium, (b) static immersion in the corrosive medium without mechanical stress, and (c) combined tribo-corrosion (sliding wear in the same corrosive medium). Measurements should be taken before, during, and after the tests.
measurements: Total weight loss of the samples
Wear track depth and surface morphology via microscopy
Analysis of the oxide layer thickness and integrity before and after testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the degradation observed in the tribo-corrosion scenario is not significantly higher than the sum of the individual degradation effects observed in the wear-only and corrosion-only tests (or if no clear disruption/regeneration interplay of the oxide layer is detected), then the proposed synergistic mechanism would be falsified.
